plans.title: Bhubaneswar · Objects and Ideas
plans.eyebrow: A flexible visit plan · choose your own pace
plans.intro: Start with something small enough to hold your attention, then a question large enough to take home. A museum object, a message in stone and a meal offer three ways into Bhubaneswar.
plans.orientation: Use Kala Bhoomi as one possible anchor and Dhauli as an optional second stop. Choose your order after checking opening arrangements, transport and your return deadline. No duration or transfer time is promised.

chapters.title: Let one object change what you notice.
chapters.text: A roof tile, a woven equation, a painted panel: our museum story invites you to look for knowledge inside an object. Choose a detail to remember rather than trying to see everything. The collection examples come from the 2019 catalogue; check what is on display now.
chapters.prompt: Confirm opening day, galleries, last entry and photography rules. Ask about seating, toilets and the approach from your drop-off point.

chapters.title: Take a question up the hill.
chapters.text: From objects made to be used, turn to words meant to guide conduct. Give the rock inscriptions and the modern Peace Pagoda separate attention. What would a promise of care mean to the people hearing it? Keep that question with you as you look.
chapters.prompt: Agree which sites you will visit and how you will reach each. Check steps, shade, seating and return pickup; do not assume the inscriptions and stupa share one entrance.

chapters.title: Let the conversation reach the table.
chapters.text: Make room for Dalma and a conversation about the meal in front of you. Ask what vegetables are in today’s preparation and what the cook enjoys serving with it. Follow the food story to meet different preparations and take a question to the table.
chapters.prompt: Choose a meal stop separately. Confirm service, ingredients, dietary needs, water and toilets; no museum café or particular restaurant is included.

preparation.title: A shorter visit
preparation.text: Choose Kala Bhoomi and a meal, or Dhauli and a meal. Remove the other stop in My journey. A single place with time to look can be a complete outing.

preparation.title: Plan the space between
preparation.text: Give a driver or host the exact stops and ask for estimates at your intended time. Add pickup, a rest and a return buffer. Check the forecast and move the outdoor part if conditions do not suit you.

preparation.title: Returning to an event
preparation.text: Work backwards from your required return time. Confirm museum arrangements first, then decide whether Dhauli fits. Your conference organiser has not approved or booked this plan.

plans.title: Cuttack · River and Silver
plans.eyebrow: A flexible visit plan · choose your own pace
plans.intro: Follow the work behind a boat, then the spaces inside a silver thread. Jobra and Tarakasi make a day of changing scale, with a bowl of Dahibara Aloodum between the conversations.
plans.orientation: Anchor the visit around a confirmed museum opening or maker appointment. Jobra, a workshop and your meal stop require separate arrangements. Reading order is not a checked driving or walking route.

chapters.title: Begin before the voyage.
chapters.text: A hull and a line of rails invite you to ask how things moved. Our Jobra story begins with the former workshop and its tools, then opens towards the waterways beyond it. Choose one machine whose purpose you want to understand.
chapters.prompt: Confirm the museum’s current hours, last entry and open galleries. Ask about access, seating and photography. The museum photographs are dated views, not a current inventory.

chapters.title: Change the scale of your curiosity.
chapters.text: After looking at a boat’s structure, follow the outline of a filigree piece. Where does the frame hold it together, and where does fine wire fill the space? A willing maker can turn a small detail into a memorable conversation.
chapters.prompt: Arrange a visit before arriving. Agree the number of visitors, time and demonstration fee, and ask before taking photographs. If a maker cannot host you, keep this as a reading stop.

chapters.title: Keep room for the bowl.
chapters.text: Soft dahibara, potato and gravy: try a little of each before bringing them together. Ask the person serving how they build their bowl. Our food story makes a small tasting game of the pause, with room for your own Cuttack memory.
chapters.prompt: Confirm ingredients, price and dietary needs before ordering. Choose a freshly prepared serving that suits you and arrange somewhere to sit and rest.

preparation.title: A shorter visit
preparation.text: Keep Jobra and a meal if no maker appointment is available. Or give a confirmed Tarakasi visit the time it deserves and save the museum for another day.

preparation.title: Travel and rest
preparation.text: Agree exact addresses, drop-off and pickup points. Ask for current transfer estimates, including your return to Bhubaneswar if needed. Leave a separate pause for water, toilets and rest.

preparation.title: For a small group
preparation.text: Check the museum’s group arrangements and how many visitors a maker can comfortably host. Agree compensation and photography consent. No group capacity, price or booking has been confirmed.

plans.title: Puri · Craft Connections
plans.eyebrow: A flexible visit plan · choose your own pace
plans.intro: A seam leads to a painted line. Follow Pipili’s cloth and Raghurajpur’s painting, then leave room for a coastal meal and the stories that stay with you.
plans.orientation: Decide which maker visit can actually be arranged before choosing the rest. Pipili and Raghurajpur are separate stops; confirm transfers and your starting point rather than treating this as a walk or a guaranteed day trip.

chapters.title: Follow the colour to a stitched edge.
chapters.text: Begin with a shape that catches your eye, then look for how it was cut and joined. Ask what the object was made for. A shop display and a working studio can offer different kinds of visit, and neither promises a demonstration.
chapters.prompt: Confirm the exact shop or host, whether a conversation is possible and any fee. Ask separately before photographing a person, workspace or design.

chapters.title: Give a painted line time to unfold.
chapters.text: Let a willing painter choose a detail to explain. Preparation, borders and fine lines offer ways into the work without asking someone to perform an entire process. Carry one question from Pipili: what changes when the pattern is painted rather than stitched?
chapters.prompt: Agree the host, visitor numbers, time and compensation in advance. A village visit does not guarantee entry to every home or a Gotipua performance. Respect a refusal.

chapters.title: Finish with a meal, not a rush.
chapters.text: Let mustard lead you into a conversation about the fish on your plate. Ask its local name and where it came from; a coastal meal may begin in freshwater. The food story introduces different preparations and questions to take to the kitchen.
chapters.prompt: Choose your eating place and confirm ingredients, mustard or fish allergies, service time and price. Plan water, seating and toilets, and leave enough time for the return journey.

preparation.title: Choose one craft if time is short
preparation.text: Keep the confirmed host and a meal. Remove the other craft stop rather than rushing a conversation. Buying an object and paying for a demonstration are separate arrangements.

preparation.title: Build around your start and finish
preparation.text: Tell your driver where you start, the exact host addresses and where you need to end. Ask for current travel estimates and a return buffer. Split the visits across days if that works better.

preparation.title: Carry the right questions
preparation.text: Ask who made a piece, how to care for it and how the maker would like to be credited. Confirm packing and any delivery terms. Discuss permission separately if you want to reproduce a design.
